content.rendered: FYI: Stack with the Strata Elite card on Citi Nights for 6x points.

Random data point. I tried using the promo codes below and even though it took the amount off, the payment would not go through on my Citi Strata Elite. It keeps giving me a “Payment could not be verified issue”. After talking with support, they advised me to remove the promo code and try again and the booking went through. Not sure if they are blocking strata cards that have used promo codes in the past but I have had 3 successfully bookings in the past with promo codes.

With the consumer Strata Elite, accelerated earnings on travel purchases are only via Citi Travel and not simply anywhere. This is part of Citi’s stated objective of pulling cardholders into its captive platform.

But, remember, hotel bookings via Citi Travel are not compatible with hotel loyalty programs. If it were, the choice would be easy. But, it’s not and it forces a choice. While the 12X is very sexy, I can generally match the total price-reward combination of a booking on another platform that is compatible with hotel loyalty programs . . . and benefits kick in. (And, the CSR’s 8X on non-Edit bookings looks anemic in comparison. Hyatt advocates will disagree.)

With a business version, other than airline elite status (I wonder which airline), I imagine it will be much the same as the consumer Strata Elite.

As for the airline elite status, just holding the card will likely afford a mostly useless tier status. Let’s say AA Gold. Then, a la Chase, upward tier steps at spending milestones. But, moving spending to the card will likely mean an opportunity cost relative to other opportunities. So, each person will need to do some math.

Many of the cards today seem to be targeting unknowing consumers who experience breakage and who experience opportunity cost. For me, after the initial “oh wow” wears off, reality (and math) sets in and my focus returns to the far simpler alternative platform.

Disappointing. 1-night-only to use these $300 credits on over-priced stays was the a saving grace for the nearly $900 AF premium card. Amex turning Platinum’s credit into 2-nights, like all of its competitors (think Chase The Edit, Citi Strata Elite, Bilt travel credits, etc.) is a devaluation. No amount of sane-washing will fix that reality. Opening up eligibility from semi-annual to annual is welcome, but doesn’t make up for the negative change. And now, for a chorus of Amex plants to tell us how they often stay more than 1 night anyway…

I can’t seem to find the terms for the points. Does anyone know if I had the Strata Elite can I still earn a bonus on the Strata Premier? Thanks

Not that it is important now, but a small correction.
You got Premier in 2022 (let’s say January), and got your bonus (no later than April-May). So 48 month rule was counting from the date you got your bonus (old rule when change of product affected the timing was gone a while ago). So you were eligible for the new Premier bonus (now Strata Premier) in May 2026.. but now – kind of never (whatever Citi’s lifetime means).

And yes, you are eligible for Regular Strata and Strata Elite. And if you downgrade Premier to Regular, that seems to disqualify you for the bonus on both (as you had both). That one is remains to be seen though.
